audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly calls Tahm Kench's W "Abyssal Voyage" and treats it as a global teleport ("threaten global pressure", "teleport ahead of him"). Tahm Kench has no global ability. His W is Abyssal Dive: a 1.35s channel, 1000/1050/1100/1150/1200 range, 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown, ending in a knockup.
audit.why: A player told to 'use Abyssal Voyage to teleport ahead of Sion' will look for a button that does not exist and lose the fight looking for it. Abyssal Dive is also cancellable during its 1.35s channel by immobilising or cast-inhibiting CC, which is the opposite of a safe escape tool.
audit.corrected: W is Abyssal Dive — a 1.35s telegraphed channel into a short blink and knockup, not an escape and not global. Sion's charged Decimating Smash will cancel it outright if you start the channel inside his swing.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: Abyssal Dive

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] calls Sion's W "Colossus W shield". Colossus is Galio's passive. Sion's W is Soul Furnace. The same line claims the shield "absorbs your empowered Devour burst", and whys[1] says the level-2 W shield "absorbs your first Devour proc" — Devour is Tahm Kench's ultimate and does not exist at level 2.
audit.why: Wrong champion's ability name, plus a timeline that cannot happen: at level 2 Tahm Kench has no ultimate, so nothing about Devour is being absorbed.
audit.corrected: Soul Furnace (W), 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown, shields for 8/10/12/14/16% of Sion's maximum health and can be recast after 3 seconds to deal magic damage scaled off the TARGET's maximum health.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states that Sion is crowd-control immune during Unstoppable Onslaught. The late-game text actively tells you to "Q-stun him before the charge" once he is already running down a lane.
audit.why: This is the single most punishing misunderstanding in the matchup. Tahm Kench's entire kit is CC — Tongue Lash stun, Abyssal Dive knockup, Devour suppression — and none of it touches a charging Sion. Only terrain collision or a champion body ends the charge; grounding disables it outright and Tahm Kench has no grounding.
audit.corrected: Sion is CC-immune for the whole of Unstoppable Onslaught (140/100/60s). Your stun, W knockup and Devour all fail on it — body-block him early or let him hit terrain.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. The text says "bait the channel" but never says what baiting actually buys you.
audit.why: Interrupting Decimating Smash mid-charge puts it on a 2-second cooldown, not its full 10/9/8/7/6s. Stunning him out of the charge therefore buys almost nothing — you have to make him release it and whiff to get a real window.
audit.corrected: Make Decimating Smash whiff rather than interrupting it: a whiff is 8-10 seconds of a Sion with no dash and no gap-close, an interrupt is two.

audit.whatIsWrong: The text tells you to out-scale Sion on HP items without noting that two of his damage sources scale off YOUR maximum health.
audit.why: Soul Furnace's recast deals magic damage based on the target's max health, and Glory in Death's on-hit does the same. Heartsteel stacking makes Sion hit you harder, which is why raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here.
audit.corrected: Sion's W detonation and zombie on-hit both scale off your maximum health — you still want HP for the frontline job, but do not expect resistances or a bigger bar to make his damage smaller.
sources: League Wiki — Sion: Soul Furnace, Glory in Death

audit.why: Sion's level-3 Q-W-E all-in, his Heartsteel first item and Tahm Kench's own Heartsteel/2-item frontline window are all correctly identified as the spikes that matter.

edits.before: Sion's first Heartsteel makes him an HP wall that laughs at your Devour damage — shift to objective control and use Abyssal Voyage to threaten global pressure while he sits top.
edits.after: Sion's first Heartsteel makes him an HP wall that laughs at your Devour damage — and Soul Furnace's recast scales off YOUR max health, so stacking HP hands him damage.

edits.before: Time Devour when Sion commits his charged Q channel — the cast time is long enough to swallow him before the knockup lands
edits.after: Make him whiff Decimating Smash rather than stunning him out of it — an interrupt refunds it in 2s, a whiff is 8-10s

edits.before: Use Abyssal Voyage to threaten bot-lane pressure whenever Sion is locked in a slow push or tower siege
edits.after: Hold Abyssal Dive until his Q is spent — its 1.35s channel is cancelled outright if his charged swing lands

edits.before: Use Colossus W shield to absorb your empowered Devour burst and pop it for AOE damage mid-trade
edits.after: Detonate Soul Furnace on you — its recast scales off your max health, so your Heartsteel feeds it

edits.before: Level 3 is Sion's best window: Q-W-E gives him a real all-in threat and his Colossus W shield absorbs your Devour proc on activation. Respect the charged Q; if you eat it and get knocked up into his W pop you will lose the trade badly. Levels 4-5 swing this lane your direction hard — Sion has no dash or gap-close, so Tongue Lash is essentially a free-hit. Walk to just outside his Q range, bait the channel, and when he cancels or commits to the wave slow him with Q and build to 3 stacks for the stun-into-Devour. At 6 his zombie passive is a nuisance in lane but your Abyssal Voyage is a genuine global threat — ping your jungler the moment Sion goes zombie so they know the wave is free to dive.
edits.after: Level 3 is Sion's best window: Q-W-E gives him a real all-in threat and Soul Furnace shields 8-16% of his max health on cast. Respect the charged Q; if you eat it and get knocked up into his W pop you will lose the trade badly. Levels 4-5 swing this lane your direction hard — Sion has no dash or gap-close, so Tongue Lash is essentially a free-hit. Walk to just outside his Q range, make him release the charge into empty ground, then slow him with Q and build to 3 stacks inside the 5s the stacks live. At 6 his zombie passive is a nuisance in lane and it heals for 100% of the damage it deals — ping your jungler the moment Sion goes zombie so nobody solo-tanks the corpse.

edits.before: Late game this becomes two immovable objects fighting for teamfight control. You win the engagement tool race — Tongue Lash stun into Devour removes a carry from a teamfight instantly, which Sion's kit cannot replicate at the same point-and-click speed. His zombie passive means you never get a clean kill on him without burning all your cooldowns first, so deprioritize the solo kill and instead use the Devour to peel your own carries or dunk their ADC. Sion will be running down a lane; use Abyssal Voyage to teleport ahead of him and Q-stun him before the charge, then let your team collapse. As long as you are ahead on HP items your grey-health pool makes you near-unkillable in the frontline and he cannot out-sustain your Thick Skin passive.
edits.after: Late game this becomes two immovable objects fighting for teamfight control. Sion will be running down a lane CC-immune — your stun, Abyssal Dive knockup and Devour all fail on the charge; body-block it or let terrain stop it. As long as you are ahead on HP items your grey-health pool makes you near-unkillable in the frontline and he cannot out-sustain your Thick Skin passive.

edits.before: Sion gets his W shield at level 2 which absorbs your first Devour proc, and you get your Devour but lack enough stacks to threaten a real all-in — neither side can force a kill.
edits.after: Sion's Soul Furnace lands at level 2 and shields 8-16% of his max health, and you have no ultimate and no stun until three stacks are up — neither side can force a kill.

edits.before: Level 6 is contested: your Abyssal Voyage adds global threat but Sion's zombie passive turns any kill attempt into a risky all-in trade; neither side gains a clean kill window.
edits.after: Level 6 is contested: Devour finally arrives but needs 3 stacks, and Sion's zombie passive turns any kill attempt into a second health bar; neither side gains a clean kill window.

edits.before: - Sion Decimating Smash: matchup-defining — Charged = knockup. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sion Decimating Smash (10/9/8/7/6s): charged 1s+ = knockup into stun. Interrupting the charge only refunds it to a 2s cooldown, so bait the whiff instead. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Decimating Smash's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Trade in the window after Decimating Smash whiffs — a real 8-9s. He has no dash, so Tongue Lash is a free hit every cooldown.

edits.before: Devour deletes him from the fight — or you from his. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Sion's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Devour needs 3 stacks and they decay 5s after your last hit. Unstoppable Onslaught is CC-immune — you cannot stun it off.

edits.before: Charged = knockup. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Charged 1s+ = knockup into stun. Engage only after he whiffs it.

edits.before: Track Sion's Decimating Smash (Stun): Charged = knockup. Dodge it. When it is down — Q-AA + R him.
edits.after: Sion is CC-immune during Unstoppable Onslaught — your stun, W knockup and Devour all fail on it.
